message.text:
q23.

SQL schema: `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (`CREATE TABLE memo`, line 33) — with the dialect twins `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql` and `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql`
Go store model: `store/memo.go` (`type Memo struct`, line 35)
API proto message: `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` (`message Memo`, line 198)
Generated frontend types: `web/src/types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb.ts`

One extra layer that matters if you're changing the shape: the `payload` column is a JSON/text blob holding a serialized `MemoPayload`, defined in `proto/store/memo.proto` and surfaced in Go as the `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` field on the store model. So structured memo metadata (tags, location, references) is defined there rather than in the SQL columns, which are just `id`, `uid`, `creator_id`, timestamps, `row_status`, `content`, `visibility`, `pinned`, and `payload`.

The Go server-side types generated from the API proto live in `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go`, and the frontend `.ts` file is generated from the same proto, so those two stay in sync automatically while `store/memo.go` and the SQL files must be updated by hand.
